title: Decisions and assumptions
body: These choices were made where the specification left room. Each can be changed. ^DEC-1
The reachability check (DOC203) is skipped when none of the roots exists, because every document would then be an orphan; DOC205 already reports the missing roots. ^DEC-2
Custom rules keep their own level when the recommended preset is switched off, because they exist only when the project defines them. ^DEC-3

The single files `docs/out.md` and `docs/out.html` take their names from the output folder (`out` and `outFull` plus an extension), so no settings exist for them. They are not checked by `docc check` and are meant to stay out of git. ^DEC-4

The single HTML file is built from the same Markdown as the single Markdown file, parsed by the library comrak with the GitHub extensions and written as HTML by docc in the form the Go version made with goldmark, and cut into blocks at markers that docc puts before every element; the marker name is chosen so that no text of the page contains it. Page anchors are the document id and field anchors are the document id, two hyphens and the field anchor. ^DEC-5
Every document has a kind schema (DOC109 is core) and the check is flat: a document is checked by the schema of its own kind only, schemas do not inherit from each other. ^DEC-6

A strict kind is closed by docc, not by `unevaluatedProperties`: the schema states a boolean `additionalProperties`, and docc collects the allowed names from the top-level properties, `allOf` branches and local `$ref` targets. This way an unknown field gets one clear message with a suggested name, instead of a validator error about a keyword the author did not write. ^DEC-7

Links carry the version hash of their target and code tags the fingerprint of their code, instead of a separate lock file: the confirmation lies next to the place that was checked, a merge shows it in the diff of that line, and nothing can be confirmed for many places at once. A link gets its hash from the agent who wrote it (or from `docc migrate`), after reading the target. ^DEC-8
Code gets a hash only inside `docc:begin` and `docc:end` regions. A hash of a whole file would warn on every unrelated edit, and warnings nobody acts on teach people to ignore them. ^DEC-9

Numbers of pages and sections are computed from the tree when `numbering` is on, so they never go out of date. Only a number typed at the start of a title or a section key is reported (DOC314); the text of fields is not checked, because a number there is part of the content. ^DEC-10
A link exists only as a reference in the text. A separate list of links would repeat the text and drift from it, and a reference in a sentence also says why the documents are related. ^DEC-11

docc is a public open source project (MIT) with releases on GitHub, installers, `docc update` and the skill installed by `npx skills add`. The first users are the author's team; there are no sales, plans or support promises. ^DEC-12

There is no command that confirms links: an agent rewrites each hash by hand after reading the change, because a command that confirms many links at once lets an agent clear errors about places nobody read. A missing or old hash is an error (DOC209, a core rule), so `docc check`, the pre-commit hook and CI stop on it. ^DEC-13

DOC209 is one diagnostic per link, because each place is checked and rewritten on its own. A link to a block or a field breaks only when that part changes; a link to a whole document breaks on any visible change of it. ^DEC-14

DOC110 warns about a free field spelled almost like a reserved key (`parnet`, `hiden`) that the kind schema does not declare. The reserved fields are the only ones with a meaning, so a typo would otherwise be silent prose. ^DEC-15

`docc build` deletes from the output folder only what it generated (pages with the GENERATED mark, copies of images that exist in the sources, file manager junk). With any other file there it refuses and lists the files, because a silent deletion loses work. A marker file and `--dry-run` were not added. ^DEC-16

A launch or config error in JSON is the usual report with a diagnostic of code `config`, `usage` or `error`, and every error of `docc.json` is listed at once, so an agent parses one shape and fixes the file in one pass. Diagnostics stay ordered errors first, then by file and position: moving warnings in among errors was not done. ^DEC-17

The history of a block comes from Git, not from a journal of docc: it covers the whole past of a project at once and adds no file. A block is one element of the JSON (a paragraph of an array, a field value), not one line of text: the elements keep their pointers when a list item is inserted inside a paragraph. Only committed states and the working tree are seen; a renamed field or section starts its history again. ^DEC-18
The HTML application uses Preact with htm in one embedded file instead of a framework with a build step, so `cargo build` stays the only build and the project needs no Node. ^DEC-19

Comments live in the documents, in a flat list `$comments`, because agents read the documents through git and a comment should travel with the text it is about. There are no statuses and no replies: a handled comment is deleted in the same commit as the fix, so the list only shrinks and the next agent sees only what is open. Only docc writes the member: `docc comments apply` edits it in place, keeping every other byte, so the CLI, the import of the HTML file and Docspace never reformat each other's files. The browser still keeps a reader's comments until they are exported, because the HTML file has no server. docc does not change the text by a comment: an agent agrees the change with a person, makes it and deletes the comment. ^DEC-20

Dictation uses the speech recognition of the browser: Chrome and Edge send the sound to their speech service. A Chromium without the keys of that service and Firefox show no microphone button; the comment is typed. ^DEC-21

docc was rewritten from Go in Rust in October 2026 for speed and type safety. The output stayed the same; every behaviour that changed is listed, with an example, in `docs/rust-port`, and the speed is in [[performance@pwkp]]. ^DEC-22

A program that shows the pages itself reads `docc compile`, not a file: it prints one JSON object and writes nothing, so a server can compile any commit, even from a bare mirror with `--rev`, without a working folder that two jobs could share. The data file `docs/out.json` of `docc build --data` was removed with it. ^DEC-23

Blocks are followed through versions by one alignment (`history::ops`): the HTML history, the block counts of `docc log`, the pairs of `docc diff` and the place a comment from an older build moves to on import come from it, so two views of the same change never disagree. Equal texts in an array match in order, the rest of a gap pairs by likeness or as a rewrite, other fields match by pointer. `docc log` counts on the JSON of each version, without compiling it, so a long history stays one `git log` and one `cat-file`; `docc diff` compiles both sides, because a reader sees includes and links resolved. ^DEC-24

In folder mode a folder's own page is the document named like the folder inside it, not `index.json`: ids stay the file names, unique in the whole project, so links and codes do not depend on where a file lies. ^DEC-25

A block code is the key of its document and a number (`^PAY-14`), not four random signs: people cite a point aloud, in chats and in code. The number is flat, not a section path like 3.2, which would lie about its place once the block moved. The next number is the largest of the document plus one, read from the files, so docc keeps no counter that two branches would conflict on; the price is that two branches can give the same number, which DOC212 reports after the merge and an agent settles, and that a deleted number can come back, which the hash of every link to it catches. ^DEC-26
The rules are listed in [[rules@kvpj]] and the settings in [[config@sbmf]]. ^DEC-27
not_verified: Windows and macOS were not run: only Linux was available. The two GitHub workflows (tests and releases) run on Linux only, so the Windows and macOS builds are cross-compiled and untested. ^DEC-28
The criterion that an agent fixes 9 of 10 synthetic errors in two iterations was not measured. ^DEC-29
